insight.title: Why Solving a Problem Makes it Look Bigger
insight.subtitle: Why your progress might look like a new setback

sections.text: When the British Army introduced steel helmets in WWI, hospital admissions for head injuries skyrocketed. Commanders were horrified, nearly banning the gear. In reality, soldiers who previously died were now surviving to be treated.
This is the "survivor’s bias" in reverse. We often measure failure by what we can see, forgetting that the most catastrophic failures are invisible because they leave no data behind to be counted.
In your work, improving a system often uncovers more errors. It looks like you are failing, but you are actually capturing data that used to be a silent, terminal disaster. Don't fear the numbers.
Try this today: When you face a new problem today, ask if it is actually a sign of hidden progress.
The absence of visible errors is often a sign of total failure, not perfect success.

news.title: China's economy grows faster than expected despite Iran war
news.description: The better-than-expected GDP data comes as Asian countries have been hit hard by the impact of the conflict.
news.why: A stronger global economy helps protect the value of your retirement savings.

news.title: 'Bit of pain' worth long-term security from Iran, Bessent tells BBC
news.description: US Treasury Secretary said a "small bit of economic pain" was worth it to eliminate the threat of Iranian strikes on Western capitals.
news.why: Security efforts could result in higher interest rates for your home loan.

news.title: UK prepares for food shortages in worst case scenario as Iran war continues
news.description: The UK could face some food shortages by the summer under a worst case scenario drawn up by government officials.
news.why: You may see empty shelves and fewer fresh options at your supermarket.

news.title: Europe has 'maybe six weeks of jet fuel left', energy boss warns
news.description: Flights could soon be cancelled if supplies from the Gulf remain blocked, says the International Energy Agency.
news.why: Your holiday flights could be cancelled as fuel supplies reach critical lows.

news.title: Russia launches deadliest aerial attack in months, killing 18 in Ukraine
news.description: A Ukrainian drone attack killed two people in Russia, Moscow says, after an Orthodox Easter truce.
news.why: Escalating war may increase the taxes you pay for national defense programs.

news.title: Snapchat owner cuts 1,000 jobs as says AI will reduce repetitive work
news.description: The Snapchat owner is laying off around 16% of staff and withdrawn hundreds of open job roles.
news.why: AI is replacing entry-level roles, changing how you compete for office jobs.

news.title: Ticketmaster-owner Live Nation ran a monopoly and overcharged fans, jury finds
news.description: The lawsuit said the firm's practices had led to higher ticket prices and worse service for customers.
news.why: You should see lower prices and fairer fees for future concert tickets.

news.title: More big energy users to get help as support plan expanded
news.description: A scheme to cut bills for firms that are heavy energy users is being extended to cover an additional 3,000 businesses.
news.why: This aid helps prevent price hikes for the essential services you use.

news.title: Cheaper Doritos and Lays helps PepsiCo win back struggling snackers
news.description: The snack giant cut some of its prices by up to 15% ahead of the Super Bowl in February.
news.why: You will pay significantly less for your favorite snacks at the checkout.

news.title: India pushes for women's quota bill as row over parliamentary seats intensifies
news.description: Southern Indian leaders urge mass mobilisation over concerns about redrawing electoral boundaries.
news.why: New quotas will give women more power over your community’s laws.

news.title: Things can't go on like this with online safety, Starmer tells tech bosses
news.description: It comes as the government continues to consult on whether to ban under-16s from social media in the UK.
news.why: Your younger family members may soon be banned from using social media.

news.title: Allbirds shares soar 580% after pivot from shoes to AI
news.description: The company is selling off its shoe brand as it plans to shift to providing technology infrastructure.
news.why: You will no longer be able to buy shoes from this brand.
